blocks.intro: An ageing system has three routes: replace one module, replace generation and keep the loop, or replace the whole package. Our options report prices each by equipment, site work and requalification, and states its downtime.

Under GMP: IQ/OQ of what changed, with agreed sampling. Without GMP: an acceptance test against your specification. Drawings and procedures updated.

items.q: Will you upgrade another maker’s system?
items.a: For makes and equipment confirmed when you enquire: we assess it, then add or replace modules. Without drawings, we walk the system down first. New piping joins yours by a method named in your proposal.

items.q: Will an upgrade restart our performance qualification (PQ)?
items.a: Not necessarily. A risk assessment sets what is retested after a change, under your change control. Your quality unit decides; we draft the rationale.

items.q: Can we keep producing water during the upgrade?
items.a: Yes, for generation, pretreatment and capacity upgrades. Each new module goes in beside the old one, tied in during a short shutdown. If your tank cannot cover it, plan temporary water from temporary units sized with you. Occupied hospitals and lab buildings stay supplied the same way. A loop replacement needs a planned shutdown.
